_comment: The continental cups that take a player AWAY DURING a league season, and which countries belong to
which confederation. DECLARED, like `classic_modules.json` and `board_rulings.json` are declared: it
is a published calendar and a published membership list, i.e. somebody else's fact that we read and
never fit. Every window below was verified against the public record on 17/08/2026 - the sources are
on each entry - because a date recalled from memory is exactly the kind of fact this project has
What it is NOT: a list of who will be called up. Nobody publishes that in August, and the engine does
not guess it - the measured penalty (`engine/cups.py`) is the AVERAGE loss of a player of that
nationality, which already contains the probability of being called at all. That is why 'ivoriano'
and 'convocato' must not be conflated: the dilution IS the measurement.
A tournament is in scope for a season when its window overlaps that season's league calendar. The
summer ones (World Cup, Euro, and from 2027 the Africa Cup) do not belong here at all: they eat a
PRESEASON, which is the `post_torneo` flag `modules/tournaments.py` already writes.
`qualified` is the final tournament's field, when it is known. Empty or absent = unknown, and then
nationality alone decides - «vuoto = ignoto», never «nobody qualified».
_exceptions_comment: The ONE thing the provider's country cannot answer: a man who holds that passport and plays for
somebody else's national team. The proxy is right 299 times out of 300 on men who played the 2026
World Cup - but that test can only see players who have already chosen, so the counter-example lives
exactly where the test is blind. A real one is in the euro sheet: Dahoud (Eintracht) reads Syria,
which is his birthplace, and has played for Germany.
Not measurable and therefore DECLARED, with the standing `board_rulings.json` has: keyed by fc_id,
dated, revocable, and it only ever REMOVES an exposure - it can excuse a man from a tournament, never
send him to one. Nothing else in the repository observes a national-team choice, so inferring it from
a birthplace would be inventing one fact from another.
`{fc_id: {reason, decided_on}}`. Empty is the normal state: it exists for the handful of names the
_confederations_comment: Country -> confederation, in the SPELLING the provider uses for a player's country (SofaScore's
`player.country.name`), because that is the string this is joined on. Validated rather than trusted:
on the 303 quoted men who played the 2026 World Cup, the provider's country matches the national team
they actually turned out for 299 times out of 300, and the single difference is a spelling (Cape Verde
/ Cabo Verde) - which is why BOTH spellings are listed here.
Only AFC and CAF are listed: they are the confederations whose senior cup has ever been played inside
a European league season. CONCACAF's Gold Cup and CONMEBOL's Copa America are summer tournaments, so a
membership list for them would be a list nothing reads.
